# A form field's bottom margin depends on which stylesheet loaded last

## Welcome 👋

A form in Neo.mjs spaces its fields with one CSS rule. Some fields set their own bottom margin with a rule of exactly the same strength, so whichever stylesheet the browser loaded **last** wins, and the same form renders two ways depending on what the app happened to create first. You'll make the outcome deterministic with one selector change, and write the browser test that proves it.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone).

## What happens today

`resources/scss/src/form/Container.scss` gives every direct child of a form `margin-bottom: 10px` through `.neo-form-container > *`, which has specificity (0,1,0). Two field roots set their own bottom margin at the same specificity:
- `.neo-textfield` sets `margin-bottom: 5px` in `form/field/Text.scss`. Number, Date, Time and the other fields that extend TextField inherit it.
- `.neo-file-upload-field` sets `margin-bottom: 2.5rem` in `form/field/FileUpload.scss`, which reserves room for its error message.

Neo loads each class's stylesheet the first time a component of that class is created (`Neo.worker.App#insertThemeFiles`). Create the form first, and `Text.css` loads after `Container.css`, so fields get 5px. Create any TextField earlier, even a hidden one, and the order flips, so the same fields get 10px. It surfaced in neomjs/neo-agent-institution#212, where a hidden card moved every field of another form by 5px.

## The fix (decided)

**The field governs.** Wrap the container's base rule in `:where()`, which contributes zero specificity:

```scss
:where(.neo-form-container) > * { margin-bottom: 10px; }   // children that set no margin of their own
.neo-form-container > *:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }   // unchanged, (0,2,0)
```

Add one comment line in the SCSS saying why: a field's own margin wins, and the container spaces only the children that set none.

**Why this option, not "the container governs"** (decided 2026-10-02 by @neo-opus-ada; @tobiu, the rule's author, was open to either):
- **It settles FileUpload too.** Its 2.5rem is a functional reserve. Under "the container governs" it would still tie with the container rule, so it needs a special case.
- **It keeps what most forms render today.** A form usually loads `Container.css` before its fields' stylesheets, so its fields already show 5px.
- **The rhythm already reads as 10px.** A form lays out as a `vbox` (flexbox), where margins don't collapse, so two stacked text fields show 5px + 5px of space.

## Where things live

- The rule: `resources/scss/src/form/Container.scss`.
- New test file: `test/playwright/component/form/Container.spec.mjs`.
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/component/form/field/Text.spec.mjs`. It loads the empty test viewport, a fresh page per test, so each test starts with no stylesheets. It creates components with `Neo.worker.App.createNeoInstance(...)`. The form's `ntype` is `form-container`, and the upload field's is `file-upload-field`.

## Done when

- [ ] `Container.scss` uses `:where(.neo-form-container) > *` for the base rule, keeps the last-child rule as is, and says why in one line.
- [ ] `Container.spec.mjs` builds the same form twice: three children, a TextField, a FileUpload field and a TextField, in that order.
  - In one test, create the form first.
  - In the other, create a standalone TextField and a standalone FileUpload field first, then the form.
  - Both tests read `getComputedStyle(...).marginBottom` and assert the same values: `5px` for the first TextField, the FileUpload field's own `2.5rem` (in px) for the upload field, and `0px` for the last child.
  - On today's `dev`, the second test fails: the first TextField reads `10px`. That's the bug, caught.
- [ ] `npm run test-components -- test/playwright/component/form/Container.spec.mjs` passes, and so does `npm run test-components`.
- [ ] The PR says which of the 10 files under `examples/` and `apps/` that import `form/Container.mjs` render differently afterwards. Only forms that ran after a TextField existed elsewhere should change. Add one before/after screenshot if any does.

## Out of scope

Other equal-specificity ties in the theme, and when or how theme files load. Insertion follows creation order by design, so the fix belongs in the selector.

## While you wait for review

You just made one rule deterministic in a multi-threaded application engine. In Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints, which is why stylesheets arrive in the order components are created. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.

## Post-Merge Validation

The maintainers check this one; the contributor doesn't. On the next neo pin bump in neomjs/neo-agent-institution, the Agent OS goldens should not move, because its forms take the form-first path. If one moves, re-capture it and say why.

Filed 2026-09-25 while fixing neomjs/neo-agent-institution#212's visual gate. Measured in the Agent OS app on Institution `dev` `d93f7db4f2` (Chromium, the visual config):
- `form/Container.css` at link index 77 and `form/field/Text.css` at 80 gave the fields 5px.
- With a TextField created earlier, Text.css moved to 29 and Container.css to 88, which gave 10px.

History: @tobiu's `a748a94664` (2020) shipped the rule in one bundle that imported `field/Text` before `Container`, so the container rule always won. Per-class theme files turned that fixed order into a race.

Precedent: #14970 made a dock rule order-independent the same way.
